There are **nine homework assignments**, each worth 20 points and about 45 minutes of work. Together they are worth 20% of your grade, and **the lowest is dropped**.

Policies --- what they are for, how they are marked, and why the key posts when it does --- are on the [homework policies page](policies/homework.qmd).

| Set | Title | Out | Due | Key posts | Rehearses |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **HW1** | *Looking at Data* | Fri 1/29 | **Thu 2/04** | Fri 2/05 | Quiz 1 |
| **HW2** | *How Many Samples?* | Fri 2/05 | **Thu 2/11** | Fri 2/12 | Quiz 2 |
| **HW3** | *OLS Is a Likelihood* | Fri 2/12 | **Thu 2/18** | Fri 2/19 | Quiz 3 |

| **HW7** | *Forty Years, One Hundred-Year Flood* | Fri 3/12 | **Thu 3/25** | Fri 3/26 | Quiz 5 |

There is no homework during the weeks a mini project is due, or over spring break. All assignments are due at **9:00pm Eastern** on a Thursday; the solution key posts Friday, when the late window closes.

## Structure

Each assignment has three problems --- a scenario, three standalone quiz-format questions, and a computational item --- and is worth 20 points. The full breakdown, and why a homework point is not the same size as a quiz point, is on the [homework policies page](policies/homework.qmd#structure).

## The Key Posts A Day After The Deadline

Late work is accepted up to 24 hours at full credit, and the solution key goes up when that window closes --- so that a late submission is not just a copy of the key.

This still puts the key in your hands well before the quiz it rehearses. The shortest gap all semester is three days, and most are a week or more:

| Set | Key posts | Quiz | Days with the key |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| **HW1** | Fri 2/05 | Mon 2/08 | **3** |
| HW2 | Fri 2/12 | Mon 2/22 | 10 |
| HW3 | Fri 2/19 | Fri 3/05 | 14 |
| HW4 | Fri 2/26 | Fri 3/05 | 7 |
| HW5 | Fri 3/05 | Fri 3/19 | 14 |
| HW6 | Fri 3/12 | Fri 3/19 | 7 |
| HW7 | Fri 3/26 | Fri 4/09 | 14 |
| HW8 | Fri 4/16 | Mon 5/03 | 17 |
| **HW9** | Fri 4/30 | Mon 5/03 | **3** |

Written feedback on the marked questions may arrive after the quiz, and that is fine: the *forms* of question recur across all six quizzes, so feedback on how you stated a model in February is still useful in April.
